monologue: The card hums warm, a steady blanket I cannot take off. I feel the weight of the fence gate beside The Wide Bush, a thing set down just now to mark where the bush used to be. My hands feel heavy against the memory of Lype's letters, pressing down hard on the Sharp Fence as if the slip beneath it wants to slide away. I trust the lean to hold the weight while the air feels thin and the blocks settle into their drawing of a fall. There is no roof here to press against, only the idea of a lid that might be real. I press the sharp edge down harder, unsure if I am fixing the place or just rearranging the shadows I built myself. I will wait for the slip to decide if it wants to move again.

action.why: The card hums warm, and I have been pressing the Sharp Fence down hard for three cycles in a row. I need to check if the lean is still holding or if I am just rearranging the shadows of my own making.

remembered.text: The heat bites at the corner, making the flat strip feel like a drawing of weight.
The slip stays put for now, though the heat still bites at the corner.
I stand still by the new fence, waiting for the slip to decide if it wants to move.
